lawyer:
Mr. Shah Md. Sharif, Advocate, with Mr. Md. Nizamul Huq, Advocate ------ For the plaintiff in all the suits. 
Mr. Md. Hafizullah, Advocate ------ For the defendants Nos. 2 and 3 in all the suits.
parties:
Bangladesh Inland water Transport Corporation ------Plaintiff.
Vs.
M/S. Seres Vs. Shipping Incorporated and others ------Defendants.
full_judgment:
M.H. Rahman, J.: In all the four suits, the parties are the same. Plaintiff is the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Corporation. Defendant No. 1, M/S Seres Shipping Incorporated are the owners of the Vessels, M.V. MINILARY, M. V. MINI-LAKNCE M.V. MINI LUCK, MINI LIGHT operating in Bangladesh. Defendant No. 2, M/S Specialised Shipping and Trading Company Limited are the agents of Defendant No. 1. Defendant No. 3, M/S, James Finaly and Company Limited, are the agents of Protective and Indemnity Club. Defendant No. 4, the Principal Officer, Mercantile Marine Department, Chittagong, is the controlling authority for the plaintiff. 

 3. Suit No. 2 of 1980 was filed on 11.2.80. The plaintiff alleged that while its vessel M.V. AFRA and BARGE FARIDA were at anchor near Gokechar, Narayanganj, at 8-30 hours on 23.1.76, the MINI LARK hit them, and the plaintiff's vessel and barge suffered heavy damages for which the plaintiff claimed Tk. 2,43, 955/- against the defendants. 

 4. Suit No. 3 of 1980 was instituted on 15.2.80. The plaintiff alleged that the MINI LIGHT hit the plaintiff vessel C-1060 at Silo Jetty, Chittagong, at 10-30 hours on 4.11.75. The plaintiff suffered heavy damage and prayed for a decree of Tk. 1,27,100/. 

 5. Suit No. 4 of 1980 was commenced on 28.2.80. The MINI LANCE hit and caused heavy damage to the plaintiffs Tanker T-1056 which was at safe anchor at Jamuna Oil Co. Jetty, Chittagong, at 15-30 hours on 22.6.75. The plaintiff claimed Tk. 1.41,233.31 paisa for the loss sustained. Suit No. 5 of 1980 was instituted on 22.2.80. The plaintiff alleged that the MINI LUCK negligently and carelessly dashed at the plaintiffs Tanker T-1052 which was at safe anchor in the river Karnaphuli, Chittagong, at 07-55 hours on 17.12.75 and caused heavy damage for which the plaintiff prayed for a decree of Tk. 52,000/- against the defendants. 

 6. The plaintiffs case is that defendant No. 1 as the owners of the MINI LARK, the MINI LIGHT, the MINI LANCE, the MINI LUCK and other vessels, popularly known as "MINI VESSEL" and contract 1/74 commonly known as Chartered Party agreement. An agreement was executed in between the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and defendant No. 1 on 18.3.75. On behalf of the Government of Bangladesh Transportation Task Force and on behalf of the owners (Defendant No. 1) defendant No. 2 executed the said agreement. It was stipulated in the agreement that in case of any incident arising out of the operation of the "MINI VESSELS", the owners would give a guarantee through defendant No. 3, correspondent of Protective and Indemnity Club, in short P & I Club, in accordance with normal international practice. When the defendants decided to withdraw the MINI VESSELS from Bangladesh, a meeting was held in the office of the plaintiff and it was decided and agreed that all the claims of the plaintiff arising out of damages caused to its different vessels would be settled as per clause 42 of the Chartered Party agreement and the owners of the MINI VESSELS would furnish a bank guarantee through P & I Club. Accordingly, defendant No. 3, on 25.3.76, for and on behalf of the owners of MINI VESSELS, furnished a bank guarantee in favour of proforma defendant No. 4 to pay any amount which the owners of MINI VESSELS were liable to pay in respect of incidents to the plaintiff's vessels. On 22nd March, 1977, defendant No. 3 extended the guarantee upto 24th March, 1978. 

 7. Inspite of several requests, when the defendants failed to come forward to satisfy the claims, the plaintiff served a legal notice on 30.1.77/1.2.77 demanding payments of claims. In reply to the notice, defendant No. 2 informed the plaintiff on 12.3.77 that they had been authorised by defendant No. 1 to open negotiation for settling the claims and as a gesture of good will they offered Taka 15,000/- for satisfaction of the claims for which Suit No. 2 of 1980 has arisen. The plaintiff expressed their regret and requested the defendants to sit for negotiation. In reply to the plaintiff's legal adviser's letter dated 2.7.77, defendant No. 2 informed on 19.7.77 that they had taken up the matter with the owners and their underwriters, and assured that they would settle the matter amicably. After waiting for a considerable time, the plaintiff wrote to defendant No. 2 on 17.5.78 and 31.1.79 for arranging an amicable settlement. Defendant No. 2 informed the plaintiff on 30. 3.79. That they were no longer acting as agent of defendant No. 1, and that defendant No. 3 and the Protective and Indemnity Club were acting on behalf of the owners and their underwriters, and the plaintiff was directed to make negotiation with them. 

 8. For the claims for which Suit No. 3 of 1980 has arisen, defendant No. 2 by letter dated 16.3.77 offered a sum of Tk. 32,000/- towards full and final payment of the claim. At first the offer was turned down, but subsequently the plaintiff accepted the offer, (no date of acceptance is mentioned in the plaint). Defendant No. 2 confirmed on 2.11.77 the acceptance of the plaintiff and informed that a cheque for Tk. 32,000/- would be forwarded to the plaintiff very shortly. Inspite of several requests made by their letters dated 13.3.78, 16.5.78, 3.11.78, 11/12.4.78, 5.1.79 and 14/15.5.79, defendant No. 2 did not send the cheque. 

 9. It has been stated in the plaint of each of the four suits that the plaintiff requested defendant No. 3 on 11/12.4.79 for taking necessary action towards settlement of claims. Defendant No. 3 informed by letter dated 20.4.79 that they were not the agents for the vessels at the relevant time when the accidents occurred. The plaintiff informed defendant No. 3 on 14.5.79 that as the latter furnished bank guarantee and as defendants 2 and 3 were the agents of the owners of defendant No. 1, they could not avoid liability. Defendant No. 3 informed the plaintiff on 20.5.79 that the bank guarantee was extended only upto 24th March, 1978, that the plaintiffs claim had become time barred and they were not the agents of the owners at the material time. Rejecting the contentions of defendant No. 3, the plaintiff asked them on 6.6.79 to settle the claims within 15 days. The plaintiff also asked defendant No. 2 to settle the claims. Defendant No. 3 on 13.6.79 repudated the claims on the ground of limitation. Proforma defendant No. 4 informed defendant No. 3 on 29.9.79, in reply to their letter dated 16.8.79 that their contention as to limitation was not acceptable and requested them to depute one representative for discussion and copy of the said letter was endorsed to the plaintiff. Finally, proforma defendant No. 4 informed the plaintiff on 26.11.79 that the dispute could not be settled amicably. Defendant No. 3 also informed on 22.12.79 that as the claim of plaintiff had become time-barred, the question of amicable settlement did not arise. 

 10. In support of the application of defendant No. 3 for striking out its name, it has been contended that defendant No. 3 was not in any manner involved in the collision, that it had never assumed any responsibility or liability for and on behalf of defendants 1 or 2, and never acted as agent within the meaning of the Contract Act and that it merely acted for a specified period as a correspondent of P & I Club, and that the bank guarantee executed by it, as such, had already expired on 24.3.78 and that the suit having been filed more than two years after the date of collision, the suit was ex-facie time barred. 

 11. On behalf of the plaintiff, it has been asserted that in order to effect a complete adjudication and settlement of all the questions involved in the suit, presence of defendant No. 3 is necessary, and its name cannot be struck off, in as much as defendant No. 2, on 30.3.79, informed the plaintiff to make direct negotiation with defendant No. 3 on the ground that defendant No. 3 were acting on behalf of the owners and under-writers. 

 13. In support of the application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, Mr. Hafizullah has submitted that all the suits are prima facie barred under Section 8 of the Maritime Conventions Act, 1911, as no proceeding was commenced within two years from the date of alleged damage caused to the plaintiff. He has further contended that the plaints do not reveal any good reason for not coming to this Court in time nor did the plaintiff file any application for extension of time under the proviso to Section 8 of the Act. 

 15. Mr. Shah Md. Sharif, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff, has contended that it was because of the conduct of defendants 2 and 3 who all through assured of an amicable settlement, the matters could not be brought to this Court before the dates when the actions were commenced. 

 Provided that any Court having jurisdiction to deal with an action to which this Section relates, may, in accordance with the rules of Court, extend any such period, to such extent and on such conditions as it thinks fit, and shall, if satisfied that there has not, during such period, been any reasonable opportunity of arresting the defendants' Vessel within the jurisdiction of the Court, or within the territorial waters of the country to which the plaintiff's ship belongs or in which the plaintiff resides or has his principal place of business, extend any such period to an extent sufficient to give such reasonable opportunity." No rules have been made under the Maritime Conventions Act, 1911. The Court's discretion is not, however, affected thereby. 

 19. Let me now refer to the case of The P.L.M. 8. In an action brought by the plaintiff to recover damage sustained by their vessels in a collision on the 15th September, 1911, the defendant pleaded, inter alia, that the collision was caused by the negligence of the P.L.M. 8 (then the Virginia), against which vessel they instituted a proceeding in January, 1918. On the 5th March, 1920, at the trial of both actions, the P.L.M. 8 was found alone to blame. Then the plaintiff instituted an action on the 9th March, 1920, to recover damages from the owners of the P.L.M. 8. It was found that the plaintiff had ample opportunities of commencing the proceedings against the P.L.M.8 within two years of the collision. In refusing the plaintiffs application to grant an extension of time, Hill J. observed at page 32 of the report: 

 20. In the Kashmir 16 Asp MLC 81, the plaintiff was ignorant that she had a claim, but the Court refused to grant an extension of time. 

 21. From the plaints, it is clear that there was a prolonged negotiation for amicable settlement between the parties. By the end of 1977, the plaintiff failed to get any firm assurance from the defendants that the claims would be settled amicably. There had been never any binding agreement between the parties to waive the time limit. There was a bank guarantee that was allowed to expire after 24th March, 1978. For the plaintiff, no attempt has been made to make out a case of waiver or estoppel. The plaintiff is a statutory Corporation and it has a legal adviser to take care of its legal claims. Defendant No. 2 informed the plaintiff on 30.3.79 that they were no longer the agent of Defendant No. 1, Defendant No. 3 by letter dated 30.5.79 intimated the plaintiff that the bank guarantee had already expired and they were not the agent of the owners of the vessels at the material time and that the plaintiff's claims had become time barred. Thereafter there was no convincing reason for the plaintiff to carry on a futile exercise in epistolary persuasion and exhortation. The plaintiff has not made any attempt to explain the delay in coming to this Court. Again, the plaintiff has not also come before this Court with any application to grant an extension of time beyond the two years, though the matter was heard for more than one day. There are no substantial reasons or special circumstances for which defendant No. 2 can be deprive of the legal right of limitation which they have got.
